# SCI-FRUIT v0.1 — EL-G0 Gate-D Readiness r0.1

Status: **Gate-D launch not ready; Gate 0 remains active pending exact owner and
human-custodian inputs**

## Readiness Matrix

| Required object | Gate-0 result | Gate-D state |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lifecycle and firewall | exact gate architecture, approval, branch preflight, and incident handling recorded | ready |
| historical recurrence source | exact commit/tree and recurrence recovered | ready as source evidence only |
| executable historical control | source build is not reproducible by commit alone; artifact/reconstruction path defined | **blocked** |
| development profiles | two candidate-neutral profiles and downstream exclusions drafted | **owner selection required** |
| finite development population | custody/split/lineage plan drafted; no inventory or custodian | **blocked** |
| qualification population protection | access and incident rules drafted; no identities opened | conceptually ready; exact population blocked |
| metrics and truth/null plan | registration families and safeguards drafted | **exact equations/priorities required before development** |
| candidate family | three-family bounded proposal drafted | **owner selection and finite grids required** |
| resource/execution plan | required fields and historical non-authoritative evidence identified | **operator and exact envelope required** |
| qualified-method record | schema available | future only |

## Present Disposition

Gate D must not launch from the current record. This is not a program no-go and
does not reject intentional-new-recurrence research. It is a fail-closed
readiness finding: the accepted baseline-relative architecture cannot operate
without an exact paired control and a protected finite population.

## Inputs Needed To Continue Gate 0

1. appoint a human historical-control/data custodian and Unity operator, or
   explicitly identify separate people for those roles;
2. authorize the custodian to return the non-outcome inventory defined in
   `EL_G0_DATA_AND_CONTROL_INVENTORY_REQUEST_R0.1.md`;
3. choose whether Gate D should prepare both generic profiles or only one;
4. choose whether the three proposed recurrence families are the permitted
   first-generation research envelope; and
5. decide whether resource limits should await the outcome-free inventory
   (recommended) or be supplied directly by the owner.

After those inputs arrive, Gate 0 can produce an exact content-bound Gate-D
candidate. Until then, no prototype, data processing, method development,
qualification, or Unity action is authorized.
